italiensk.explanation: "Italiensk" means "Italian". It comes from "Italien" (Italy). To name the language, use it as the language: "Jeg taler italiensk" (I speak Italian).

ivrig.explanation: "Ivrig" means "eager". To say someone does a hobby with great energy, put it before the noun: "en ivrig cyklist" (a keen cyclist).

iøjnefaldende.explanation: "Iøjnefaldende" means "conspicuous". It comes from "at falde i øjnene" (literally, to fall into the eyes).

at jage.explanation: "At jage" means "to hunt / chase". To say someone runs after a person to catch them, use it for the chase: "Politiet jager tyven" (The police chase the thief). To say someone hunts wild animals, use it for the hunt: "Han jager hjorte" (He hunts deer).

at jamre.explanation: "At jamre" means "to wail / whine". To say what someone complains about, put "over" (about) after it: "Han jamrer over vejret" (He whines about the weather).

at juble.explanation: "At juble" means "to cheer". It is the verb for the noun "en jubel" (jubilation). To say when people cheer, add a sentence with "når" (when): "Folk jubler, når holdet scorer" (People cheer when the team scores).

at justere.explanation: "At justere" means "to adjust". Do not copy the "ad" of "adjust": the Danish word starts with "ju". To say you change a plan a little, put the plan after it: "Vi justerer planen" (We are adjusting the plan).

en jagt.explanation: "En jagt" means "a hunt". It is the noun for the verb "at jage" (to chase). To talk about looking hard for something, use "jagten på" (the hunt for): "jagten på en bolig" (the hunt for a home).

en jakke.explanation: "En jakke" means "a jacket". To talk about a long, warm coat instead, use "en frakke" (a coat): "Jeg tager frakken på" (I put my coat on).

en japaner.explanation: "En japaner" means "a Japanese person". To describe things from Japan, use "japansk" (Japanese) instead: "japansk te" (Japanese tea).

en jobannonce.explanation: "En jobannonce" means "a job ad". It is built from "job" (job) and "en annonce" (an ad).

en jobsamtale.explanation: "En jobsamtale" means "a job interview". It is built from "job" (job) and "en samtale" (a conversation). To say you are going to one, use "til" (to): "Jeg skal til jobsamtale" (I am going to a job interview).

en joke.explanation: "En joke" means "a joke". To say you tell one, use "at fortælle" (to tell): "Han fortæller en joke" (He tells a joke). To say you are not serious, use "at lave sjov" (to kid around): "Jeg laver bare sjov" (I am just joking).

en jomfru.explanation: "En jomfru" means "a virgin / maiden". To name the mother of Jesus, use it in "Jomfru Maria" (the Virgin Mary). To name the star sign, use "Jomfruen" (Virgo).

en jordemoder.explanation: "En jordemoder" means "a midwife". It is built from "jord" (earth) and "moder" (mother). In Denmark, a "jordemoder" leads a normal birth, and a doctor joins only if there are problems.

en jordnød.explanation: "En jordnød" means "a peanut". It is built from "jord" (ground) and "en nød" (a nut).

en journal.explanation: "En journal" means "a medical record". To say a diary instead, use "en dagbog" (a diary): "Jeg skriver i min dagbog" (I write in my diary).

en journalist.explanation: "En journalist" means "a journalist". To name the job, put "som" (as) before it: "Hun arbejder som journalist" (She works as a journalist).

en juleferie.explanation: "En juleferie" means "a Christmas vacation". It is built from "jul" (Christmas) and "ferie" (vacation). To say you are on vacation, use "ferie" as its own word: "Jeg har ferie" (I am on vacation).

en julefrokost.explanation: "En julefrokost" means "a Christmas lunch". It is built from "jul" (Christmas) and "frokost" (lunch). In Denmark, a "julefrokost" is a big get-together in December with food and drinks.

en julegave.explanation: "En julegave" means "a Christmas present". It is built from "jul" (Christmas) and "en gave" (a gift). To thank someone for any gift, use "gave" as its own word: "Tak for gaven!" (Thanks for the gift!)

en julemand.explanation: "En julemand" means "a Santa Claus". It is built from "jul" (Christmas) and "mand" (man). To make other Christmas words, put "jul" in front: "et julekort" (a Christmas card).

en julemiddag.explanation: "En julemiddag" means "a Christmas dinner". It is built from "jul" (Christmas) and "middag" (dinner). To talk about a Christmas lunch party instead, use "en julefrokost" (a Christmas lunch): "Vi har julefrokost på arbejdet" (We have a Christmas lunch at work).

en julesang.explanation: "En julesang" means "a Christmas carol". It is built from "jul" (Christmas) and "sang" (song). The part "sang" also appears in "en børnesang" (a children's song).

en julestjerne.explanation: "En julestjerne" means "a poinsettia". It is built from "jul" (Christmas) and "en stjerne" (a star). To talk about a star decoration, it also means "a Christmas star": "Vi hænger en julestjerne op i vinduet" (We hang a Christmas star in the window).
